title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 51 (Payment of Dividend in Proportion to Amount Paid-Up)

content.overview: Section 51 provides that a company may, if so authorised by its articles, pay dividends in proportion to the amount paid-up on each share.
content.glance: If articles authorise, dividends may be paid in proportion to the amount paid-up on each share.
content.study: A company may, if so authorised by its articles, pay dividends in proportion to the amount paid-up on each share (s. 51). The provision is enabling only: proportional payment is available where the articles so authorise and becomes relevant where shares have different amounts paid-up. Declaration and payment of dividend must still comply with the other applicable provisions of the Act (including section 123). Current-law framing: check the articles for authorisation; if authorised, apply dividend in proportion to the amount paid-up on each share; otherwise follow the articles and general dividend rules.

sections.heading: Articles authority
sections.body: Proportional dividend is available only if the articles of the company authorise it.

sections.heading: Proportion to amount paid-up
sections.body: Where authorised, the company may pay dividends in proportion to the amount paid-up on each share (relevant where paid-up amounts differ).

provisions.title: Payment of dividend in proportion to amount paid-up

examples.title: Proportional dividend
examples.body: Articles authorise proportional dividend. Shares with ₹50 paid-up receive half the dividend per share of fully paid ₹100 shares. Section 51 is applied.

examples.title: No articles authority
examples.body: Articles are silent. The company cannot rely on s. 51 to pay dividend only in proportion to paid-up amounts without articles authorisation.

hypotheticals.question: Must dividends always be proportional to paid-up capital?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only if the articles authorise it under s. 51. Otherwise the company’s dividend distribution follows the articles and general dividend rules.

distinctions.title: Proportional dividend (s. 51) vs acceptance of unpaid capital (s. 50)
distinctions.left: How dividend may be calculated on shares with different paid-up amounts
distinctions.right: Power to accept uncalled capital in advance

misconceptions.trap: Partly paid shareholders always get reduced dividend by force of statute alone.
misconceptions.correction: Section 51 applies only if the articles authorise proportional dividend.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 51 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Check whether the articles authorise proportional dividend. II. Compare paid-up amounts on the relevant shares. III. If authorised, apply dividend in proportion to amount paid-up. IV. Confirm compliance with other dividend provisions (e.g. s. 123). V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Articles clause; paid-up amounts; proposed dividend calculation; precise relief.

examTips: Proportion is to amount paid-up, not nominal value alone.
Other dividend rules (s. 123 etc.) still apply.
